gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 9 build route is visible on current master beside `zigux/kernel/runtime_loader.zig`, `zigux/kernel/runtime_loader_contract.zig`, `zigux/tests/runtime_loader_allocator_init_flow.zig`, and `zigux/tests/runtime_loader_gap_survey.zig`, but it remains review-only evidence until the broader runtime substrate exists.
The dedicated runtime survey gate keeps the direct sample packet and the visible shared-loader reminder packet fail-closed instead of implying live runtime parity.
The dedicated `make -C zigux phase9-runtime-atomic64-test` route keeps the direct atomic64 pilot-module packet replayable on current master beside the visible shared loader-facing reminder packet.
The bounded sample keeps the direct atomic64 starter and guarded lifecycle parity evidence reviewable under the `lib/atomic64_test.c` anchor.
The sample descriptor and `runSelftest()` contract keep the roadmap selftest hook surface explicit without implying a live runtime substrate.
The dedicated module tests keep the bounded starter lifecycle and direct sample-backed module gate reviewable on current master.
The narrow diff gate keeps add, sub, bitwise, swap, compare-swap, and add-unless expectations from `lib/atomic64_test.c` machine-checkable without widening the runtime packet.

A bounded loader scaffold keeps the entry and exit symbol names, handoff-plan shape, and the adjacent shared loader-facing reminder packet reviewable without implying live runtime registration parity.
The roadmap's full runtime module lifecycle parity still depends on the broader runtime substrate beyond the current direct atomic64 packet and visible shared loader-facing reminder packet.
